headline: A 2022 law extends two federal child exploitation programs through fiscal year 2024.
what_it_does: The law reauthorizes two federal efforts through fiscal year 2024. The first is the National Strategy for Child Exploitation Prevention and Interdiction. The second is the National Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force Program. The official summary covers only these two programs, so this explanation does not describe any other parts of the law.

who_it_affects.group: State and local law enforcement agencies that take part in the Internet Crimes Against Children task forces
who_it_affects.how: Their participation in the federal task force program continues through fiscal year 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that carry out the national strategy to prevent and stop child exploitation
who_it_affects.how: They keep their authority to carry out the strategy through fiscal year 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Children who may be targets of online exploitation
who_it_affects.how: The two federal programs aimed at preventing and stopping this exploitation stay in place through fiscal year 2024.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 21, 2022, and the reauthorization runs through fiscal year 2024, which ends September 30, 2024.
